answer: Sybil resistance here rests on a stake-weighted admission bond. Registering an identity means locking a minimum native-token deposit in escrow while it stays active; the protocol weights identity by that capital, not by key count. A puppet copies the full escrow cost, and rewards split by weight, so doubling identities halves each share while doubling funds at risk. A proven cluster forfeits every member's bond. An island deployment with an onyx or copper reserve tier applies the same rule, so a sybil estate costs its smallest funded member each time, growing with capital, not cheap keys.
